intent: Compare the Bank of England base rate and the example five-year fixed mortgage rate over the period from 1991 to 2016 to determine how each changed.

requirements.question: Are all required line series shown in every declared panel?
How did the Bank of England base rate change from 1991 to 2016?
How did the example five-year fixed mortgage rate change from 1991 to 2016?
How do the changes in the two rates compare over the period?

units.claim: All 2 required series appear in panel single chart.
accept: every required series is visible and correctly labeled in this panel
reject: series assigned to the wrong panel

units.claim: The Bank of England base rate fell from 10.1996% in 1991 to 0.3991% in 2016, a decrease of 9.8005 percentage points.
accept: Base rate decreased by about 9.8 percentage points from 1991 to 2016
reject: Base rate increased over the period
Base rate ended higher than it started

units.claim: The example five-year fixed mortgage rate fell from 9.4989% in 1991 to 2.1996% in 2016, a decrease of 7.2993 percentage points.
accept: Mortgage rate decreased by about 7.3 percentage points from 1991 to 2016
reject: Mortgage rate increased over the period
Mortgage rate ended higher than it started

units.claim: Both the Bank of England base rate and the example five-year fixed mortgage rate decreased from 1991 to 2016, with the base rate falling by a larger absolute amount (9.8005 percentage points) than the mortgage rate (7.2993 percentage points).
accept: Both rates fell over the period
Base rate fell by more percentage points than the mortgage rate
reject: One rate increased while the other decreased
Mortgage rate fell by more than the base rate

optional_valid: The base rate reached a minimum of 0.3991% in 2016.
The mortgage rate reached a minimum of 2.1996% in 2016.
unsupported_to_avoid: Causal explanations for the rate changes.
Claims about intermediate years not shown in the basis rows.
Percentage change comparisons unless explicitly computed from the table.
review_notes: The mortgage rate first row has an empty x value in the table summary; point_order 1 is used as the 1991 starting point based on the series x_values listing 1991 as first.
The intent asks to determine how each changed and to compare them; three semantic units cover the two individual changes and the cross-series comparison.
